title: Beatrix and the Ghost
premise: Ulyana Crane, a financial-crimes investigator who launders her own past under clean money, is approached by a stranger named Beatrix who claims Ulyana once saved her life — a favor Ulyana has no memory of. The debt comes with interest: intelligence about an attack planned to look like an industrial accident during an upcoming economic summit, orchestrated by the very institution that trained Ulyana to erase people like herself. As Ulyana investigates, she discovers her missing memories were not lost but taken, and that Beatrix may be the one person who knows what Ulyana did to survive. In the end, Ulyana must choose between exposing the plot and preserving the lie that keeps her alive — stopping the attack by sacrificing the polished identity she built, walking away from her old life as the summit's 'accident' becomes a public scandal instead.
about_author: Theo Yarrow is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people whose careful lives are built on things they'd rather forget.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. We meet her meticulous double life: spotless investigator by day, packed bag and forged passport in the closet by night. A routine audit of a shipping firm turns up a payment routed through an account that shouldn't exist — hers, or nearly hers. Beat: unease beneath control.

chapters.title: A Favor Returned
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A woman calling herself Beatrix appears at Ulyana's apartment, thanking her for saving her life in Riga three years ago — a city Ulyana has no record of visiting. She leaves a burner phone and a warning: interest is owed. Beat: vertigo; the first crack in the polished lie.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with a flashback fragment of Riga she can't verify. She pulls her own travel records and finds them too perfect, scrubbed with the same technique she uses at work. Someone erased her, using her own tradecraft. Beat: dread sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix explains the debt: the favor was real, and repayment means helping her stop an attack timed for the Meridian Summit, designed to read as a gas-main accident. Ulyana refuses — until Beatrix shows her a photo from Riga with Ulyana's face in it. Beat: cornered.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Following the money, Ulyana maps a chain of shell entities feeding a private security contractor, Halvern Group, which holds the summit's infrastructure contract. Her supervisor, Denny Marsh, notices her queries and warns her off gently. Beat: the hunt begins; loyalty starts to feel like surveillance.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Flashback to Riga: Beatrix drowning after a botched job, pulled out by a stranger with Ulyana's eyes and a different name. Beatrix has spent three years finding her. Beat: tenderness entangled with debt; we learn Beatrix's motives are not pure.

chapters.title: Marsh
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Denny invites her to lunch and mentions Riga unprompted, watching her reaction. He offers her a promotion contingent on dropping the Halvern thread. Ulyana realizes her own agency may be inside the machine she's investigating. Beat: betrayal dressed as kindness.

chapters.title: Ninety-Six Hours
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix lays out the timeline: the attack hits during the summit's opening gala, ninety-six hours out, killing dozens and burying evidence of Halvern's fraud in the rubble. She needs someone who can read the money fast. Ulyana commits. Beat: reluctant alliance sealed.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Digging into her own erasure, Ulyana finds the program that did it — an internal witness-protection-for-the-guilty scheme called Ghost, run through Halvern. Her memories weren't lost; they were archived as leverage. Beat: horror at recognizing her own handwriting in the redactions.

chapters.title: The Safehouse
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Hiding in a safehouse, the two women trade truths over cheap wine. Beatrix admits she chose Ulyana partly for the debt, partly because Ulyana's archived file can burn Halvern down. Ulyana admits she doesn't want to know what she did in Riga. Beat: intimacy built on mutual blackmail.

chapters.title: Follow the Contractor
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Tracing Halvern's subcontractors, Ulyana finds the physical vector: a firm with access to the summit venue's utility tunnels, paid in increments that spike around the gala date. The accident has a schedule. Beat: cold clarity; the thriller engine engages.

chapters.title: Denny's File
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana breaks into Denny's office and finds her own Ghost archive — including the Riga operation, where she didn't just save Beatrix; she burned a whole network to cover her escape, and Beatrix was collateral who survived. Beat: devastating self-recognition; the price of survival made visible.

chapters.title: Confrontation
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix confronts Ulyana with what she now knows Ulyana knows: Beatrix's crew died because of her. The debt was never gratitude — it was a long-planned reckoning wrapped around a real emergency. Beat: rage and grief; the alliance fractures.

chapters.title: Both Hostages
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Halvern's cleaners find them; the safehouse is compromised. A chase through the old port district ends with Beatrix shot covering Ulyana's escape — repaying the favor in blood, whether she meant to or not. Beat: action peak; guilt inverted.

chapters.title: Triage
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Hiding Beatrix in a clinic off the books, Ulyana works alone against the clock: forty hours to the gala. She drafts two endings — expose Halvern quietly and vanish, or blow it open publicly and end her own life as Ulyana Crane. Beat: exhausted resolve.

chapters.title: The Archive
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana retrieves her full Ghost file from a Halvern data vault using credentials she shouldn't still have — proof the program existed, and that the attack is insured fraud: Halvern stands to collect on the summit's disruption clause. Beat: the motive clicks; everything converges.

chapters.title: Denny's Choice
chapters.summary: Denny's POV. Denny, revealed as a mid-level Ghost handler who genuinely liked Ulyana, is ordered to clean up the Ulyana problem. He hesitates, then tips her off about the tunnel access schedule — his one act of conscience. Beat: complicity and its small redemption.

chapters.title: Gala Eve
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. With Beatrix feverish but lucid, they plan the intervention: seal the tunnels, trigger the failsafe inspection, and get the archive to three journalists simultaneously so no one can bury it. Ulyana packs her go-bag one last time. Beat: quiet before the storm; farewell to her old self.

chapters.title: The Accident That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Summit night: Ulyana trips the inspection lockdown minutes before the charge detonates, containing the blast in an empty service corridor while the archive hits the wires. Halvern's operators scramble; Beatrix, from a wheelchair ramp, identifies the lead fixer to police. Beat: climax — chaos, precision, near-failure.

chapters.title: Interest Paid
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. In the aftermath, Beatrix tells Ulyana the debt is settled — not forgiven, but paid. She gives Ulyana the last piece of the Riga file and disappears, leaving the choice of what to do with it. Beat: release without absolution.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Facing congressional investigators, Ulyana testifies to Ghost and Halvern, confessing her own role in Riga — trading her polished lie for the truth's protection. Her career, her name, her clean money all burn. Beat: costly integrity; the theme lands.

chapters.title: Unpacked
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, epilogue. Months later, living under her real name in a coastal town with nothing packed and nothing polished, Ulyana receives a postcard with no signature — just a tide chart for Riga. She smiles, files it away, and leaves the closet empty. Beat: survival redefined; hard-won peace.
